hints: First expand $2\sin(x-30^\circ)$ using the sine subtraction formula.
Collect the expression as $\sqrt3\sin x-2\cos x$ and compare it with $R\sin(x-\alpha)$.
Match $R\cos\alpha=\sqrt3$ and $R\sin\alpha=2$ to find exact $R$ and acute $\alpha$.
walkthrough:
Apply the compound angle formula $\sin(A - B) = \sin A\cos B - \cos A\sin B$ to expand $2\sin(x - 30^\circ)$:
$$2\sin(x - 30^\circ) = 2(\sin x\cos 30^\circ - \cos x\sin 30^\circ)$$

Substitute the exact values $\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$2\sin(x - 30^\circ) = 2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x\right) = \sqrt{3}\sin x - \cos x$$

Subtract $\cos x$ and collect like terms:
$$2\sin(x - 30^\circ) - \cos x = (\sqrt{3}\sin x - \cos x) - \cos x = \sqrt{3}\sin x - 2\cos x$$

Equate this expression to $R\sin(x - \alpha) = R(\sin x\cos\alpha - \cos x\sin\alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\sin x - (R\sin\alpha)\cos x$:
$$\text{Coefficient of } \sin x: \quad R\cos\alpha = \sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{Coefficient of } \cos x: \quad R\sin\alpha = 2$$

Determine the exact value of $R$ by squaring and summing both equations:
$$R^2 = (R\cos\alpha)^2 + (R\sin\alpha)^2 = (\sqrt{3})^2 + 2^2 = 3 + 4 = 7$$
Since $R > 0$:
$$R = \sqrt{7}$$

Determine $\alpha$ by dividing the two equations:
$$\tan\alpha = \dfrac{R\sin\alpha}{R\cos\alpha} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$$
$$\alpha = \arctan\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \approx \arctan(1.1547005) \approx 49.1066^\circ \approx 49.11^\circ$$

hints: Replace the left side by the R-form from part (i) and solve $\sin(x-\alpha)=1/\sqrt7$.
Find both sine branches over the shifted interval, then retain only values satisfying $0^\circ<x<180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the $R$-form established in part (i) into the equation:
$$2\sin(x - 30^\circ) - \cos x = 1 \implies \sqrt{7}\sin(x - 49.11^\circ) = 1$$

Find the principal reference angle:
$$\theta_{\text{ref}} = \arcsin\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\right) \approx \arcsin(0.377964) \approx 22.21^\circ \quad (\text{more precisely, } 22.20765^\circ)$$

Establish the allowable interval for the compound argument $x - 49.11^\circ$ given $0^\circ < x < 180^\circ$:
$$-49.11^\circ < x - 49.11^\circ < 180^\circ - 49.11^\circ = 130.89^\circ$$

Evaluate the possible angles in this interval:
- First quadrant solution:
$$x - 49.1066^\circ = 22.2077^\circ \implies x = 22.2077^\circ + 49.1066^\circ = 71.3143^\circ \approx 71.3^\circ$$
- Second quadrant solution:
$$x - 49.11^\circ = 180^\circ - 22.21^\circ = 157.79^\circ$$
$$x = 157.79^\circ + 49.11^\circ = 206.9^\circ$$
Since $206.9^\circ > 180^\circ$, this second value lies outside the specified interval and is rejected.

State the unique solution rounded to 1 decimal place:
$$x = 71.3^\circ$$
